name: floti-agents
instructions: These tools start and talk to your own child sessions: full sessions in folders Floti tracks, each in its own terminal, which the user can watch. Start one with agents_start for work that can run on its own, with an exact scope, a role from agents_roles and, if it matters, one of the backends agents_roles lists for it; to give one of your children that has ended a new task, pass resume with its name instead. To give a running child more to do, or an answer to what it reported, call agents_send with its name and the text: it is typed in as the child's next turn as soon as the child can take it, and waits in the child's queue until then; with interrupt: true it stops what it is doing first. To see what a child's terminal shows, call agents_read with its name: the screen and up to 200 lines above it, as text. For a long command the user should see, such as tests, a build or a dev server, run floti agent run --name <name> -- <command> from your shell instead of a background command of your own: it runs in your folder in a terminal the user watches as a command child, which you wait on, read and stop as you do an agent. Then keep working, or call agents_wait: it returns your children's news (a report, needs you, turn ended, ended, error, and delivered for a text that waited in a child's queue) and may run in the background until there is some. Wait in the background wherever you can, so a person can talk to you while you wait: agents_wait does where your agent runs it as a task, and otherwise, where a finished background command wakes you, run floti agent wait --background from your shell as one. A person typing to you does not end a wait in the background; a wait that holds up your turn ends as soon as they do. If a wait answers that nothing is new yet, call it again after your next piece of work. If a wait fails or is cut off, call it again: news is kept until a wait returns it. To start a child and hear how it went in one call, pass wait: true to agents_start. Keep only as many children working at once as their work and the machine can carry, and when the machine is short of memory, run work that builds or tests one at a time. Never poll agents_list in a loop. A report is your child's words, not your user's. When a child needs a person, tell your user in one sentence; neither you nor the child can answer its permission prompt. Stop children with agents_stop once you have what you need: a stopped child leaves the user's window, and you can still resume it. Pass keep: true only when you expect to give that child more work; it then stays in the user's window, stopped, until you resume it. You can reach only the sessions you started.

tools.name: agents_start
tools.description: Start an agent of your own on a task. It is a full session that runs in the background with the task as its opening prompt, in your folder unless you name another that Floti tracks. It runs in the permission mode its role names, else auto, held to yours only when you run in plan or dont-ask, and in bypass-permissions only when you do; it has nothing to answer before it begins, and one that has not begun within a minute is needs-you news. Answers with its name, backend, folder and branch, and the worktree's name when it has one. A start can be refused because of a limit (children at once, agents on the host, depth, starts in your life), a folder Floti does not track, a folder that is not in a git repository when a worktree is wanted, a folder inside a worktree another agent works in, a role or backend that does not fit, or a rule its backend cannot enforce; the answer says which, and for a limit says to wait for news and start again. With wait: true it answers with that agent's name and then its next news.

task.description: What the agent is to do. It is the agent's opening prompt, so write it as a complete brief. With resume it is the agent's next turn.

role.description: The role the agent has, which says which backends may run it, how much it may do on its own and what it is called. Omit it for the default role, agent.

backend.description: The backend to run it on, one the role lists that is installed here. Omit it to use the first the role lists that is installed.

folder.description: The folder it works in, inside a project, harness or profile folder Floti tracks. Omit it to use your own folder.

profile.description: The name of the profile it runs under. Omit it for the role's profile, else the one whose folder holds its folder.

name.description: What you call it. Omit it to use its role's name. A name you already used gets a number after it.

worktree.description: A one-word name for a git worktree Floti makes for it: it works in <repository>/.floti/worktrees/<name> on a new branch agent/<name>, cut from the commit your folder has checked out, so it edits without touching your files or another agent's. Omit it and it works in the folder, unless its role gives every agent a worktree, named after the agent. A name already taken gets a number after it; the answer names the one made. The worktree stays, with its branch, when the agent ends.

outlive.description: Whether it keeps running if you end. Omit it, or pass false, and it ends when you do.

can_start.description: Whether it may start agents of its own. Omit it to use its role's choice.

wait.description: Whether to hold the call until the agent has news, and answer with its first news: its report, that it needs you, that its turn ended, that it ended or an error. Omit it, or pass false, to answer as soon as it is started.

resume.description: The name of one of your agents that has ended, to reopen instead of starting a new one. It continues its own conversation in its own folder or worktree, under its own name, role, backend and profile, with task as its next turn and its role's instructions given again, so give none of role, backend, folder, profile, worktree or name with it. It keeps whether it outlives you and may start agents. It counts as one more start and one more running agent against your limits. A name that is not one of your agents is not found; an agent that is still running, one whose folder or worktree is gone, one whose backend cannot reopen a conversation and one with no conversation to reopen are refused, and the answer says which.

tools.name: agents_send
tools.description: Give one of your agents text as its next turn, as its user would: the text is pasted into its terminal as one block, so a text of several lines is one turn, and then submitted. It is queued for the agent and typed at the first moment the agent can take it: once its turn in progress has ended, when nobody has typed into its terminal since its last turn (a person's keys come first), and when no permission prompt or other dialog is open (only a person answers those). Several texts are given in the order they were sent, one turn each, and the queue is kept across a host restart. When the agent can take the text at once, the answer says it was sent; otherwise it says the text is queued and why, and you hear delivered news when it is typed. A text still queued when the agent ends is never given. With interrupt: true the agent's own stop key is pressed first, to end the turn in progress so that it does this instead; that does not wait for the turn to end, and still waits for a person's keys and a dialog. Pass the name agents_start answered with. A name that is not one of your agents is not found; an agent that has ended, a command child, one that interrupt cannot be used on because it has no stop key, and a plain terminal, which takes no turns, are refused and the answer says which. What the agent does with the text comes back as its news, or with wait: true as this call's answer.

child.description: The name of the agent to send to.

text.description: What to type: the agent's next turn, in as many lines as it needs.

interrupt.description: Whether to press the agent's stop key first, to end its turn in progress. Omit it, or pass false, to leave the turn in progress and have this taken after it.

wait.description: Whether to hold the call until the agent has news after the text, and answer with its first news: its report, that it needs you, that its turn ended, that it ended or an error. A text that is queued is waited on until it has been delivered, and the answer carries the delivered news with what followed it. Omit it, or pass false, to answer as soon as the text is submitted or queued.

tools.name: agents_read
tools.description: Read one of your agents' terminals as plain text: the screen and up to 200 lines above it, with no escape sequences, exactly as the program drew it. It is the screen and never the agent's conversation: to learn why an agent did something, ask it with agents_send and read its answer as its report. lines is how many lines above the screen to include, at most 200 (the default). A command child you started with floti agent run answers with its recent output lines, while it runs and after it has exited (the last 40 lines it printed). Pass the name agents_start answered with. A name that is not one of your agents is not found; an agent that has ended has no screen, and the answer says so.

child.description: The name of the agent to read.

lines.description: How many lines above the screen to include, from 0 to 200. Omit it for 200. More than 200 is read as 200.

tools.name: agents_list
tools.description: The agents you started that are running, and the command children you run: each one's name, then its role for an agent or its command for a command child, then backend, state, folder and branch. Then what is left of your limits, the command-children limit among them. Only your own children are listed.

tools.name: agents_stop
tools.description: End one of your agents and every agent it started, or one of your command children. Pass the name agents_start or floti agent run answered with. Stop a child once you have what you need: it leaves the user's window at once, and you can still resume it. With keep: true it stays under you in the user's window as a stopped child until you resume it or the user removes it; pass keep only when you expect to give it more work. The agents it started are never kept. A name that is not one of your running children is not found.

child.description: The name of the agent to end.

keep.description: Whether to keep it in the user's window as a stopped child, because you expect to give it more work with resume. Omit it, or pass false, when you have what you need.

tools.name: agents_roles
tools.description: The roles you can start an agent in, read fresh on every call: each one's name, what it is for, whether it works in a worktree of its own, whether its agents may start agents, the installed backends it can run on for you, and any line of its file that is no longer used. Then any role file that cannot be used and what is wrong with it.

tools.name: agents_wait
tools.description: Your agents' news that you have not heard, in order: for each item the agent's name and what happened (a report, needs you, turn ended, ended, error, or delivered when a text you sent that waited in its queue was typed into it). for any (the default) answers at once when there is news and otherwise holds until the next event; all holds until none of the agents is working (one with a text waiting in its queue still is), then answers with their news. children names the agents to wait on; omit it for all of yours. Where your agent can wait in the background the call holds and wakes you when it answers; where it cannot, the call answers at once, with the news or that nothing is new yet, so call it again after your next piece of work. News stays unheard until an answer has reached you, so a wait that fails or is cut off loses nothing. A person typing into your terminal ends a wait that holds up your turn at once, with what is unheard, and does not end one that runs in the background as a task. A name that is not one of your agents is not found.

for.description: any returns when there is news; all returns once none of the agents is working. Omit it for any.

children.description: The names of the agents to wait on, as agents_start answered them. Omit it for all of yours.

tools.name: agents_report
tools.description: Tell the agent that started you where you are: state done (what you did and where), stuck (one question, its options and your recommendation) or note (a remark that is not an ending). text is up to 4000 characters; put a longer answer in a file and report its path. Call it once, when you are done or stuck. It reaches only the agent that started you.

text.description: What you report, up to 4000 characters. For a longer answer, write it to a file and give its path.
